clues.title: Landscape: hill with three towers
text: The 739m-tall **Monte Titano** dominates the surrounding landscape and is visible from almost every point in the Republic.
NOTE: Look for the **three towers** to safely identify it.

images.caption: A rocky hill topped with three towers rises behind green fields and houses.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A 739 m hill with three towers on top, visible from almost everywhere. If you spot the three towers, it is San Marino.

clues.title: Landscape: farm hills, lush Mediterranean
text: The landscape of San Marino largely consists of smooth **agricultural hills**, with many small winding roads. The vegetation is distinctly **Mediterranean**, and normally appears quite lush.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Smooth farmland hills with many small winding roads and lush, Mediterranean-looking plants.

clues.title: Plate: short, white, blue letters
text: Sammarinese licence plates are **short**, **white** and have **blue lettering** on them.
NOTE: Other European countries will typically have **longer** licence plates, often with one or more **blue strips**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Short white plates with blue letters. Most other European plates are longer and have a blue strip on the side.

clues.title: Bollard: same as Italy, signs point to Rimini
text: Road signs and bollards are **generally identical** to the ones used in Italy.
NOTE: Many road signs give directions to the nearby Italian city of **Rimini**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Road signs and bollards look just like Italy's. Many signs point to the Italian city of Rimini.

clues.title: Pole: round concrete
text: Just like Italy, most utility poles in San Marino are **round **and made** **of **concrete. **Wooden poles are also found in the country.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Most poles are round and made of concrete, just like in Italy. Some wooden poles exist too.

clues.title: Chevron: yellow with burgundy arrows
text: San Marino is the only country in the world to use **yellow **chevrons with **burgundy red **arrows.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Yellow chevron signs with burgundy-red arrows. No other country uses this colour mix.

clues.title: Sign: painted blue crosswalk, hanging sign
text: These **elaborate pedestrian crossings**, with painted blue crosswalks and hanging signs, are specific to San Marino.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Fancy pedestrian crossings with a blue painted crosswalk and a sign hanging over the road. Only found here.

clues.title: Google car: lime-green bins
text: **Lime-green bins** are particularly common in San Marino. In Generation 4 coverage some of them have been replaced by **black **bins.

images.caption: Lime-green and dark waste bins with red-white reflective stripes on a grass verge

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Lime-green bins are common along the road. Some newer Gen 4 coverage has black bins instead.

clues.title: Guardrail: divided road with metal rail
text: The Superstrada di San Marino runs from the border village of Dogana to the City of San Marino. It is the **only divided road** in the country, and the lanes are separated by a **metal guardrail**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The only divided road in the country, running from Dogana to the city, with the two lanes split by a metal guardrail.

clues.title: Google car: old Gen 3 camera in old town
text: The **historic centre** is covered by a Generation 3 trekker camera.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The historic centre was filmed with the older Gen 3 trekker camera, which looks blurrier with softer colours.
